questions.q: What are the main characteristics of living things?
answer: Living things are distinguished from non-living things by showing a set of life processes together.

answer.text: They need food for energy and growth — plants make their own by photosynthesis, animals depend on others — and they respire to release energy from that food.
They grow in size over time and show movement — animals move from place to place, and even plants move, for example towards light.
They respond to stimuli, remove waste by excretion, and reproduce to produce young of their own kind.
Finally, every living thing is born, grows and eventually dies, completing a life cycle.

questions.q: What is meant by stimulus and response? Explain with examples, and state why a moving car is not living.

answer.text: A stimulus is a change in the surroundings that causes a living thing to react, and the reaction itself is the response. For example, the touch-me-not (Mimosa) plant folds its leaves when touched, our pupils narrow in bright light, and roots grow towards water.

answer.lead: Why a car is not living.
answer.text: A car moves, but movement is only one feature. Living things must show all the characteristics of life together — nutrition, respiration, growth, response, excretion and reproduction. A car does none of these on its own, so despite moving it is non-living.

answer: This is why a single feature such as motion cannot decide whether something is alive.
